bug_description.original: The color conversion input does not check for the correct size of the alpha plane in the relevant function, which can lead to a security vulnerability.
bug_description.normalized: In libheif, an attacker-controlled HEIF file can supply an auxiliary alpha image whose decoded plane is smaller than the primary image. The decode path transfers that smaller plane into the primary HeifPixelImage as heif_channel_Alpha, and heif::convert_colorspace later treats alpha-channel presence as sufficient without checking that the alpha plane has full image resolution. Op_RGB_to_RGB24_32::convert_colorspace then iterates over the primary image dimensions and reads past the smaller alpha buffer.

source.description: During primary-image decode, the attacker-controlled auxiliary alpha image is decoded into a separate HeifPixelImage. The witness survives parsing far enough that this nested decode succeeds and materializes the smaller alpha plane that later becomes img's Alpha channel.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled HEIF auxiliary-image bytes referenced by alpha_image; this nested decode creates the alpha plane buffer and geometry that later reach the crashing read.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: The conversion loop reads alpha bytes with the primary image's full width and height, even though the transferred alpha plane is smaller. This reads one byte past the alpha buffer and ASan reports a heap-buffer-overflow read at this line.

root_cause.description: Color conversion decides whether to preserve/use alpha based only on channel presence. It does not validate that input->get_width(heif_channel_Alpha) and input->get_height(heif_channel_Alpha) match the full image dimensions before the pipeline runs. The fix adds this full-resolution alpha-plane check and rejects mismatched inputs.

tainted_value_origin.description: The nested decode of the attacker-controlled auxiliary alpha image materializes the smaller plane buffer and dimensions that later propagate into img as heif_channel_Alpha.

parser_admitted.description: By this point the HEIF file has parsed successfully, the primary image has an associated auxiliary alpha image, and decoding has entered the path that materializes the alpha plane later used by color conversion.

fine_trace.note: The parsed HEIF input carries an auxiliary alpha image, so alpha_image is non-null here. Decoding that auxiliary image materializes a separate HeifPixelImage whose Y plane becomes the alpha data for the primary image. ASan's allocation stack later shows the overflowing buffer came from this nested decode via HeifPixelImage::add_plane.

The decoded Y plane from alpha is moved into the main image as heif_channel_Alpha without copying or resizing it. The main img keeps its own full-image width and height, while the transferred Alpha plane keeps the smaller buffer and per-channel dimensions decoded from the auxiliary image.

The fuzz target requests YCbCr/420 output, and this call executes because the decoded image state differs from that target. Color conversion therefore runs on img after step 2 has already attached the smaller Alpha plane.

Conversion setup treats the mere presence of heif_channel_Alpha as enough to preserve and use alpha. It never compares input->get_width(heif_channel_Alpha) or input->get_height(heif_channel_Alpha) against the main image dimensions before the pipeline later runs. The fix adds exactly that validation.

fine_trace.code: int width = input->get_width(); int height = input->get_height();
fine_trace.note: The crashing conversion stage, identified by ASan frame 0, takes its loop bounds from the primary image's overall width and height. These are the full image dimensions, not the per-channel width and height of the transferred Alpha plane.

Because the image still has an Alpha channel, the operation retrieves the alpha-plane pointer and stride from input. That pointer still refers to the smaller auxiliary-image buffer transferred in step 2.

The nested loops iterate over the full width and height from step 5, then read alpha at x + y*in_a_stride from the smaller buffer loaded in step 6. When x,y reach coordinates that exist in the primary image but not in the transferred Alpha plane, this expression reads past the end of that buffer. ASan observed a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read immediately past a 4111-byte region allocated for the auxiliary plane.

poc.trigger: Running the staged HEIF PoC through libheif's `file-fuzzer` reproduces an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read in `Op_RGB_to_RGB24_32::convert_colorspace` at `libheif/heif_colorconversion.cc:164`.

format.name: HEIF
format.contract: A HEIF file that parses far enough to decode both the primary image and its referenced auxiliary alpha image, where the decoded alpha plane is smaller than the primary image but is still transferred into the primary HeifPixelImage as `heif_channel_Alpha` before colorspace conversion runs.
